reply: Yes, a small fix belongs in claude-settings. The local triage worked from a stale copy of the roadmap branch: git only updates that copy on a fetch. The guard refuses its push before git reaches GitHub, so the refusal could not say the commit was already there, and the session asked you to push work you had already pushed, twice. Filed step roadmap-push-refusal-says-fetch: the refusal tells the session to fetch and to ask you only when the commit is missing. It adds no network call to the hook. The fuller fix is debt local-triage-tier-proof, which lets local triage push. Triage, 21:31 CST.

The mistake was mine. Twice now I asked you to push a commit you had already pushed. My copy of the roadmap branch only updates when I run git fetch. After you pushed, I didn’t fetch, so I still thought the commit was missing. The guard refuses my push before git ever contacts GitHub, so the refusal didn’t tell me either.

claude-settings doesn’t really need a fix. The cause is a step I skipped, and one fetch before each ask covers it. A small help would be for the guard’s refusal to check GitHub and say “this commit is already on the branch”. That only matters while local triage sessions can’t push, and the planned fix to the tag gap (debt debt/local-triage-tier-proof) removes that whole situation.
